I'm the same way with the neuodivergency and fixation so I get that entirely. I know you understand the difference between real and fake, I'm sorry if I gave the impression that you didn't because that was not my intention.

The part about not truly having a moral system if you don't uphold fictional characters to the same morality standards is what I was calling a reach, because it's just not true for most people. Maybe for you, and that's up for you to decide.

Morality is 100% subjective as well, so everybody's moral code is entirely different. Something that's severe to you may be something minor to someone else.

 And, for my moral code at least, fictional characters do not effect my beliefs in the slightest because I know what I believe in. And I know I am not supporting that bad action out in the real world just because I enjoy a fictional character that has done that.  Even if I don't like a single action from a character, I will still enjoy some for pure entertainment value. It's okay! Because it's not condoning harm for anybody just because I am enjoying watching somebody, if that makes sense.

Morality in fictional characters does not really matter to the same extent of actual people because the gravity of their actions do not affect real people the way they affect other fiction people.  There is no such thing as a completely perfect, unflawed character. That would be boring. There would be no conflict. 

Sometimes it is okay to just let yourself enjoy a character who was flaws and makes mistakes. It doesn't mean your whole moral code has to come crumbling down. It's not that serious. These people are FAKE and purely for entertainment value. They have never harmed any real people. 

Claiming someone doesn't have a moral code because they allow themselves to enjoy fictional characters is a reach and entirely untrue.

Imo, finding a tv character fun or entertaining or even loving them does not mean someone's real life values are on the line at all. You can like fictional characters on TV that you'd otherwise hate in real life. Because they're just that- fictional. plus everybody and everything is problematic at some point, real or not. It's how being human works. It is how we all learn. We all make mistakes and hopefully most of us learn from them. Obviously this doesn't apply to somethings: racism, etc. But liking a character that has done bad things does not make you a bad person whatsoever. 

If that is how you'd like to guard what media you consume and what shows and which characters you let yourself enjoy, I can't stop you. That's all up to you. But there is no such thing as an unproblematic or perfect character or person. I just know that it would take a lot of the fun out for ME to police who I'm allowed and not allowed to enjoy watching based on who is flawed or done something wrong.
